title: Iconic World Landmarks & Wonders
description: 36 original questions on ancient wonders, UNESCO sites, bridges, towers, and mosques with vector silhouettes.
author: QuizRooms

questions.prompt: Which ancient Egyptian wonder illustrated here is the oldest and only surviving Wonder of the Ancient World?
questions.explanation: Built for Pharaoh Khufu around 2560 BC, the Great Pyramid stood as Earth's tallest structure for 3,800 years.

questions.prompt: Which ivory-white marble mausoleum in Agra, India, is illustrated here?
questions.explanation: Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan commissioned the Taj Mahal in 1632 for his wife Mumtaz Mahal.

questions.prompt: Which sail-shaped architectural masterpiece in Australia is illustrated here?
questions.explanation: Designed by Danish architect Jørn Utzon, it opened on Sydney Harbour in 1973.

questions.prompt: Which iconic Roman amphitheater in Italy is illustrated here?
questions.explanation: Completed in 80 AD, the Colosseum could hold over 50,000 spectators.

questions.prompt: Which famous Art Deco suspension bridge spanning San Francisco Bay is illustrated here?
questions.explanation: Opened in 1937, its signature red-orange color is officially called 'International Orange'.

questions.prompt: In which country is the ancient Nabataean rock-cut city of Petra located?
questions.explanation: Petra's Treasury (Al-Khazneh) is carved directly into rose-red sandstone cliffs.

questions.prompt: Which monumental fortification stretches over 21,000 km across northern China?
questions.explanation: Built across multiple dynasties, the most famous stone sections date from the Ming Dynasty.

questions.prompt: In which country is the 15th-century Inca citadel of Machu Picchu located?
questions.explanation: Machu Picchu sits 2,430 meters above sea level in the Peruvian Andes.

questions.prompt: Which towering Art Deco statue overlooks Rio de Janeiro from Mount Corcovado?
questions.explanation: Completed in 1931, the soapstone-clad statue stands 30 meters tall excluding its pedestal.

questions.prompt: Which country gifted the Statue of Liberty to the United States in 1886?
questions.explanation: Designed by Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi with an internal frame engineered by Gustave Eiffel.

questions.prompt: In which city is the unfinished basilica Sagrada Família, designed by Antoni Gaudí, located?
questions.explanation: Construction began in 1882 and continues more than 140 years later.

questions.prompt: Which ancient Greek temple dedicated to Athena crowns the Acropolis of Athens?
questions.explanation: Built in the 5th century BC, the Parthenon is a pinnacle of Doric architecture.

questions.prompt: In which country is the vast 12th-century temple complex of Angkor Wat located?
questions.explanation: Angkor Wat is the largest religious monument in the world.

questions.prompt: Which prehistoric ring of standing stones stands on Salisbury Plain in England?
questions.explanation: Stonehenge aligns with the sunrise of the summer solstice and sunset of the winter solstice.

questions.prompt: In which city does the historic Hagia Sophia stand?
questions.explanation: Completed in 537 AD under Emperor Justinian, Hagia Sophia is famed for its massive dome.

questions.prompt: Which Moorish palace and fortress complex overlooks Granada, Spain?
questions.explanation: The Alhambra is celebrated for its intricate Nasrid stucco calligraphy and courtyards.

questions.prompt: Which Mayan stepped pyramid at Chichén Itzá in Mexico is dedicated to the feathered serpent god Kukulcán?
questions.explanation: During equinoxes, shadows cast a descending serpent down its staircase.

questions.prompt: Which fairy-tale 19th-century Bavarian castle inspired Disney's Sleeping Beauty Castle?
questions.explanation: Commissioned by King Ludwig II of Bavaria in 1869.

questions.prompt: Which famous leaning freestanding bell tower stands in Tuscany, Italy?
questions.explanation: It began leaning during construction in the 12th century due to soft clay soil.

questions.prompt: Which ancient wonder of the world stood in Alexandria, Egypt, guiding ships with fire and mirrors?
questions.explanation: Built on Pharos Island in the 3rd century BC, it stood over 100 meters tall.

questions.prompt: In which city is the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque, one of the largest mosques in the world, located?
questions.explanation: Completed in 2007, it features 82 white marble domes and over 1,000 columns.

questions.prompt: Which skyscraper in Dubai has been the world's tallest building since 2009 (828 meters)?
questions.explanation: Burj Khalifa has 163 habitable floors.

questions.prompt: In which country are the colossal carved stone heads known as Moai found?
questions.explanation: The Moai were carved by the Rapa Nui people on Easter Island, a special territory of Chile.

questions.prompt: Which iconic suspension bridge in London opens its bascules to let tall ships pass along the Thames?
questions.explanation: Completed in 1894, Tower Bridge is frequently mistaken for London Bridge.

questions.prompt: Which ancient Roman temple in Rome features the world's largest unreinforced concrete dome with a central oculus?
questions.explanation: Rebuilt by Emperor Hadrian around 126 AD, its dome is 43.3 meters in diameter.

questions.prompt: In which country is the Great Mosque of Djenné, the largest mud-brick building in the world, located?
questions.explanation: Every year the community gathers for the Crépissage festival to replaster its adobe walls.

questions.prompt: Which ancient city in Tunisia preserves one of the largest and best-preserved Roman amphitheaters outside Italy?
questions.explanation: The Amphitheatre of El Djem could seat around 35,000 spectators.

questions.prompt: Which famous Buddhist stupa in central Java, Indonesia, is the largest Buddhist temple in the world?
questions.explanation: Built in the 9th century, Borobudur features nine stacked platforms and 504 Buddha statues.

questions.prompt: In which country are the rock-hewn monolithic churches of Lalibela carved downward from solid volcanic tuff?
questions.explanation: The 11 medieval churches of Lalibela include the cross-shaped Church of Saint George.

questions.prompt: Which towering twin skyscrapers in Kuala Lumpur were the world's tallest buildings from 1998 to 2004?
questions.explanation: They remain the tallest twin towers in the world at 451.9 meters.

questions.prompt: Which grand imperial palace complex in central Beijing was home to Ming and Qing emperors?
questions.explanation: The Forbidden City contains 980 surviving buildings across 72 hectares.

questions.prompt: Which hilltop palace in Lhasa, Tibet, served as the historic winter residence of the Dalai Lama?
questions.explanation: Standing at 3,700 meters elevation, Potala Palace is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

questions.prompt: Which ancient Roman aqueduct bridge in southern France is famous for its three tiers of stone arches?
questions.explanation: Built in the 1st century AD, Pont du Gard carried water 50 km to Nîmes.

questions.prompt: Which monumental mountain sculpture in South Dakota depicts four US presidents?
questions.explanation: Carved between 1927 and 1941, it portrays Washington, Jefferson, Roosevelt, and Lincoln.

questions.prompt: Which iconic cathedral on Red Square in Moscow is famous for its colorful onion domes?
questions.explanation: Commissioned by Ivan the Terrible in the 1550s.

questions.prompt: In which country is the ancient desert oasis city of AlUla and the Nabataean site of Hegra (Madain Salih) located?
questions.explanation: Hegra was Saudi Arabia's first UNESCO World Heritage Site.
